items.stem: Explain the term “squamous epithelium”.
items.answer: A single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries, found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries, found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as type of muscle tissue or specialised connective tissue: blood, cartilage, cardiac muscle, skeletal muscle.
items.answer: blood – specialised connective tissue; cartilage – specialised connective tissue; cardiac muscle – type of muscle tissue; skeletal muscle – type of muscle tissue.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: blood – specialised connective tissue; cartilage – specialised connective tissue; cardiac muscle – type of muscle tissue; skeletal muscle – type of muscle tissue.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a specialised connective tissue?
items.answer: smooth muscle
items.markingKey: (a) Smooth muscle is a type of muscle tissue, not a specialised connective tissue.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Ligaments attach muscles to bones.”
items.answer: Ligaments attach bone to bone; tendons attach muscle to bone.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Ligaments attach bone to bone; tendons attach muscle to bone.

items.stem: Give two differences between ciliated epithelium and squamous epithelium.
items.answer: Ciliated epithelium: lines bronchioles; moves particles or mucus in a specific direction. Squamous epithelium: found in air sacs of lungs; single thin layer of flattened cells.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. ciliated epithelium – lines bronchioles; moves particles or mucus in a specific direction; squamous epithelium – found in air sacs of lungs; single thin layer of flattened cells.

items.stem:
Om injured his knee playing cricket in Chandigarh. The doctor said a band joining his thigh bone to his shin bone was torn, though the muscles and their attachments were fine.
(i) What tissue joins one bone to another? (1 mark)
(ii) What attaches muscles to bones? (1 mark)
(iii) Classify these tissues and state the main fibre that gives them strength. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Ligament. (ii) Tendon. (iii) Dense regular connective tissue; collagen fibres arranged in parallel bundles between rows of fibroblasts.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between ciliated epithelium and squamous epithelium on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An animal tissue shows these features: lines bronchioles. Identify the tissue – ciliated epithelium or squamous epithelium? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Ciliated epithelium: columnar or cuboidal cells bearing cilia; moves particles or mucus in a specific direction; lines bronchioles. Squamous epithelium: single thin layer of flattened cells; irregular cell boundaries; lines walls of blood vessels. (b) Ciliated epithelium.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: ciliated epithelium; 1 mark: “lines bronchioles” is a feature of ciliated epithelium.

items.stem: Which of the following is a type of muscle tissue?
items.answer: cardiac muscle
items.markingKey: (a) Cardiac muscle is a type of muscle tissue; the others are not.

items.stem: An animal tissue shows these features: free surface may have microvilli; nuclei located at the base; lines the stomach and intestine. Identify the tissue. Give a reason.
items.answer: Columnar epithelium
items.markingKey: 1 mark: columnar epithelium; 1 mark: the features free surface may have microvilli; nuclei located at the base; lines the stomach and intestine are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which term describes dense regular connective tissue that attaches one bone to another?
items.answer: ligaments
items.markingKey: (c) Ligaments: dense regular connective tissue that attaches one bone to another.

items.stem: An animal tissue shows these features: present beneath the skin; serves as a support framework for epithelium. Identify the tissue. Give a reason.
items.answer: Areolar tissue
items.markingKey: 1 mark: areolar tissue; 1 mark: the features present beneath the skin; serves as a support framework for epithelium are characteristic of it.

items.stem:

Reason (R): Smooth muscle is voluntary.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Smooth muscle is involuntary; skeletal muscle is voluntary.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Name the three types of cell junctions found in epithelia and give the function of each.
items.answer: Tight junctions – stop leakage of substances across the tissue; adhering junctions – cement neighbouring cells together; gap junctions – connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes large molecules.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about animal tissues is correct?
items.answer: Bones have a hard, non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres.
items.markingKey: (c) Bones have a hard, non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres. The other statements are false. Smooth muscle is involuntary; skeletal muscle is voluntary. Cartilage cells are chondrocytes; bone cells are osteocytes. Ligaments attach bone to bone; tendons attach muscle to bone.
options: Bones have a hard, non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between ciliated epithelium and columnar epithelium on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An animal tissue shows these features: lines the stomach and intestine. Identify the tissue – ciliated epithelium or columnar epithelium? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Ciliated epithelium: columnar or cuboidal cells bearing cilia; moves particles or mucus in a specific direction; lines bronchioles. Columnar epithelium: single layer of tall, slender cells; nuclei located at the base; free surface may have microvilli. (b) Columnar epithelium.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: columnar epithelium; 1 mark: “lines the stomach and intestine” is a feature of columnar epithelium.

items.stem: Classify connective tissues with examples. Describe the structure of bone and cartilage.
items.answer: Loose (areolar, adipose), dense (regular – tendons, ligaments; irregular – skin), specialised (cartilage, bone, blood). Cartilage – solid pliable matrix of chondroitin salts, chondrocytes in lacunae; nose tip, ear, vertebrae. Bone – hard, non-pliable matrix rich in calcium salts and collagen, osteocytes in lacunae; bone marrow produces blood cells; main structural support.
items.markingKey: 2 marks classification; 3 marks bone and cartilage.

items.stem: What is meant by “epithelium”?
items.answer: A tissue that has a free surface facing a body fluid or the outside environment and covers or lines some part of the body.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a tissue that has a free surface facing a body fluid or the outside environment and covers or lines some part of the body.

items.stem: Explain the term “poikilotherm”.
items.answer: An animal whose body temperature varies with the temperature of the environment, like the frog.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an animal whose body temperature varies with the temperature of the environment, like the frog.

items.answer: (i) Males; vocal sacs. (ii) External. (iii) Tadpole; metamorphosis.

items.answer: A is false, but R is true.

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.stem: Describe the digestive and respiratory systems of the frog.
items.answer: Digestive: mouth, buccal cavity, bilobed tongue to capture prey, pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, intestine, rectum, cloaca; short alimentary canal (carnivore); liver and gall bladder (bile), pancreas (pancreatic juice); digestion in stomach and intestine; absorption by villi and microvilli. Respiratory: in water by skin (cutaneous respiration); on land by buccal cavity, skin and lungs (pulmonary respiration); lungs are a pair of elongated pink sacs; during aestivation and hibernation by skin.
items.markingKey: 2½ marks each.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Frogs have external ears.”
items.answer: The tympanum receives sound; there is no external ear.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The tympanum receives sound; there is no external ear.

items.stem: Which term describes the membrane that protects the frog's eyes while it is in water?

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the morphology and anatomy of the frog is correct?

options: Fertilisation in the frog is internal.
The frog heart has four chambers.
Fertilisation in the frog is external and development involves a tadpole larva.
Adult frogs excrete mainly uric acid.

items.answer: The summer sleep of frogs to protect themselves from extreme heat.

items.answer: buccal cavity – part of the frog's digestive system; rectum – part of the frog's digestive system; conus arteriosus – part of the frog's circulatory system; stomach – part of the frog's digestive system.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: buccal cavity – part of the frog's digestive system; rectum – part of the frog's digestive system; conus arteriosus – part of the frog's circulatory system; stomach – part of the frog's digestive system.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct levels of organisation from simplest to most complex: tissue, organism, organ system, cell. Give a reason.
items.answer: cell → tissue → organ system → organism
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order cell → tissue → organ system → organism; 1 mark for the reason: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems.

items.stem: Explain the term “organ”.
items.answer: A structure made of two or more types of tissues organised to perform a specific function, such as the stomach or heart.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a structure made of two or more types of tissues organised to perform a specific function, such as the stomach or heart.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Adipose tissue is located mainly beneath the skin.
Reason (R): Adipose cells are specialised to store fats.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (b) Both true; location is not explained by fat storage.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following is a part of the frog's circulatory system?
items.answer: sinus venosus
items.markingKey: (c) Sinus venosus is a part of the frog's circulatory system; the others are not.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Smooth muscle is voluntary.”
items.answer: Smooth muscle is involuntary; skeletal muscle is voluntary.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Smooth muscle is involuntary; skeletal muscle is voluntary.

items.stem:
An organ system of the frog is described: brain in a bony brain box (cranium); ten pairs of cranial nerves; divided into fore-brain, mid-brain and hind-brain.
(i) Identify the system. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the digestive system? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The nervous system (ii) central, peripheral and autonomic divisions (iii) short alimentary canal as frogs are carnivores; liver secretes bile stored in the gall bladder
items.markingKey: (i) the nervous system – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: central, peripheral and autonomic divisions – 1 mark. (iii) for the digestive system: short alimentary canal as frogs are carnivores; bilobed tongue used to capture prey; liver secretes bile stored in the gall bladder – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about organ and organ systems in animals is correct?
items.answer: The stomach wall contains epithelial, connective, muscle and neural tissue.
items.markingKey: (b) The stomach wall contains epithelial, connective, muscle and neural tissue. The other statements are false. An organ is made of two or more types of tissues. All functions in unicellular organisms are carried out by a single cell. Organ systems are interdependent and coordinated by neural and hormonal systems.
options: Organ systems function independently of one another.
The stomach wall contains epithelial, connective, muscle and neural tissue.
Each organ is made of only one type of tissue.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the morphology and anatomy of the frog is incorrect?
items.answer: Adult frogs excrete mainly uric acid.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “Adult frogs excrete mainly uric acid.” Correct form: Adult frogs are ureotelic and excrete urea.
options: The frog does not drink water but absorbs it through the skin.
Fertilisation in the frog is external and development involves a tadpole larva.
Adult frogs excrete mainly uric acid.
Male frogs have vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs.

items.stem: What is meant by “neuroglia”?
items.answer: Cells of neural tissue that protect and support neurons and make up more than half the volume of neural tissue.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cells of neural tissue that protect and support neurons and make up more than half the volume of neural tissue.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between the digestive system and the circulatory system on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An organ system of the human body has these components and functions: alimentary canal and associated glands. Identify the system – the digestive system or the circulatory system? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) The digestive system: alimentary canal and associated glands; breaks down complex food; absorbs nutrients. The circulatory system: heart and blood vessels; transports nutrients, gases and wastes; blood and lymph are its fluids. (b) The digestive system.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: the digestive system; 1 mark: “alimentary canal and associated glands” is a feature of the digestive system.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a type of muscle tissue?
items.answer: areolar tissue
items.markingKey: (d) Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue, not a type of muscle tissue.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Organ systems function independently of one another.”
items.answer: Organ systems are interdependent and coordinated by neural and hormonal systems.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Organ systems are interdependent and coordinated by neural and hormonal systems.

items.stem: Which of the following is a dense connective tissue?
items.answer: ligaments
items.markingKey: (d) Ligaments is a dense connective tissue; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct levels of organisation from simplest to most complex?
items.answer: cell → tissue → organ system → organism
items.markingKey: (b) cell → tissue → organ system → organism. Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems.

items.stem: Define the term “urinogenital duct”.
items.answer: The common duct in the male frog that carries both urine and sperms (Bidder's canal leads into it).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the common duct in the male frog that carries both urine and sperms (Bidder's canal leads into it).

items.stem:
An animal tissue shows these features: serves as a support framework for epithelium; contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells; loose arrangement of cells and fibres.
(i) Identify the tissue. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were cardiac muscle? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Areolar tissue (ii) present beneath the skin (iii) involuntary contraction; present only in the heart
items.markingKey: (i) areolar tissue – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: present beneath the skin – 1 mark. (iii) for cardiac muscle: present only in the heart; branching pattern of cells; intercalated discs – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as loose connective tissue or type of muscle tissue: cardiac muscle, areolar tissue, skeletal muscle, smooth muscle.
items.answer: cardiac muscle – type of muscle tissue; areolar tissue – loose connective tissue; skeletal muscle – type of muscle tissue; smooth muscle – type of muscle tissue.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: cardiac muscle – type of muscle tissue; areolar tissue – loose connective tissue; skeletal muscle – type of muscle tissue; smooth muscle – type of muscle tissue.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about organ and organ systems in animals is incorrect?
items.answer: Each organ is made of only one type of tissue.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “Each organ is made of only one type of tissue.” Correct form: An organ is made of two or more types of tissues.
options: In multicellular animals, organs work together to maintain homeostasis.
Each organ is made of only one type of tissue.
The heart contains all four types of tissues: epithelial, connective, muscular and neural.
